pull.title: MINOR: Fix the refiner's restored-something check
pull.body:
A member reports a task position of 0 before it restores anything, and
Long.MAX_VALUE only when the offset sum overflows. hasRestoredSomething
incorretly read MAX_VALUE as "restore not started", so a fresh warm-up
counts as started. This patch fixes this bug.

Follow up to
https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23519#discussion_r4120294506

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body:
### 🟢 Approval recommended The focused predicate correction matches client offset reporting, and regression tests cover the affected behavior with no unresolved findings. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR This PR corrects how the Streams assignment refiner detects restore progress, so a fresh warm-up reporting position zero no longer counts as having restored data. **Changes:** - Require a positive reported position to indicate restore progress, including overflow values of `Long.MAX_VALUE`. - Clarify offset-reporting documentation and update regression tests for indexing and warm-up preemption. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | group-coordinator/​src/​test/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​coordinator/​group/​streams/​AssignmentRefinerTest.java | Updates zero-position, unknown-offset, overflow, and preemption coverage. | | group-coordinator/​src/​main/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​coordinator/​group/​streams/​AssignmentRefinerImpl.java | Corrects the restore-progress predicate and clarifies offset semantics. |
Review effort: Balanced

LGTM, with 2 nits for your consideration.

The semantics for the lags are really a bit confusing, especially the inclusive vs. exclusive behavior of restore offsets.

review_comments.body: nit: this reads as if there's one value per changelog, but it's the sum of the positions over all of the task's changelogs. Maybe something like "it reports a changelog position sum above 0 for it, which is 0 only while it has restored nothing from any of its changelogs"?

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -983,9 +983,11 @@ private static PatchedTasks patchFor( * own predicate, so that both ends agree on when a warm-up task is caught up. * *

The lag is the distance between the reported end offset and the reported offset, and a lag that is not known - * is never within the threshold: an offset missing on either side, or capped at {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} to say that - * the restore has not started, counts as not caught up. A slightly negative lag does count, because the offset is a - * position while the end offset is the last offset, so a fully restored task reports a lag of -1. + * is never within the threshold: an offset missing on either side, or reported as {@link Long#MAX_VALUE}, counts as + * not caught up. The client reports an end offset of {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} while it does not know a changelog's end + * offset yet, and either offset as {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} when its sum over the changelogs overflows. A slightly + * negative lag does count, because the offset is a position while the end offset is the last offset, so a fully + * restored task reports a lag of -1.
review_comments.body: nit: the end offset isn't always the last offset. `StoreChangelogReader#logicalChangelogEndOffsets` returns `restoreEndOffset` when it's set, which is exclusive (log end offset / committed offset), so a fully restored task reports a lag of 0 there. Only the `storeMetadata.endOffset()` fallback is a last offset and gives -1. Doesn't change the result since both are within the threshold, but maybe reword to "a lag of 0 or -1"?

The lag is the distance between the reported end offset and the reported offset, and a lag that is not known - * is never within the threshold: an offset missing on either side, or capped at {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} to say that - * the restore has not started, counts as not caught up. A slightly negative lag does count, because the offset is a - * position while the end offset is the last offset, so a fully restored task reports a lag of -1. + * is never within the threshold: an offset missing on either side, or reported as {@link Long#MAX_VALUE}, counts as + * not caught up. The client reports an end offset of {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} while it does not know a changelog's end + * offset yet, and either offset as {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} when its sum over the changelogs overflows. A slightly + * negative lag does count, because the offset is a position while the end offset is the last offset, so a fully + * restored task reports a lag of -1.
review_comments.body: Yes, it's annoying that `storeMetadata.endOffset()` is the last actual offset introducing an off-by-on issue... That's what `A slightly negative lag does count` refers too -- because we sum it up, it's not necessarily 0 or -1, but could also be -k if we have changelog partitions for a task. Let me reword.

A member reports a task position of 0 before it restores anything, and
Long.MAX_VALUE only when the offset sum overflows. hasRestoredSomething
incorretly read MAX_VALUE as "restore not started", so a fresh warm-up
counts as started. This patch fixes this bug.

The lag is the distance between the reported end offset and the reported offset, and a lag that is not known - * is never within the threshold: an offset missing on either side, or capped at {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} to say that - * the restore has not started, counts as not caught up. The client reports an end offset of {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} while it does not know a changelog's end + * offset yet, and either offset as {@link Long#MAX_VALUE} when its sum over the changelogs overflows. issue.body:
This PR completes the first version of the refiner. In addition to the
main wiring, this PR also fixes a bug in load handling, and improves how
warm-up tasks are planet.

Part of KIP-1071.
